To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of cytotoxic thiosemicarbazonates and phenoxazines results not only in a significant reduction in the dose of the thio-semicarbazone but also in a significant reduction of the cytotoxic potential against normal cells.

the combination of cytotoxic thiosemicarbazonato copper( ii ) complexes with phenoxazine derivatives results in a synergistic enhancement in cytotoxicity, with an enhanced selectivity against cancer cells, which is attributed to the generation of reactive oxygen species.

the combination of cytotoxic thiosemicabazone complexes with phenothiazines or phenoxazines results, in some instances, in up to 50–fold enhancement in the cytostatic and/or cytotoxic potential of thiosemicarbazonates against MCF-7 cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis and evaluation of copper–thiosemi-carbazone complexes and phenoxazines in the development of novel anticancer therapeutics.
the discovery and evaluation of novel redox active combination therapies that are effective against human breast adenocarcioma cells while minimizing toxicity against normal fibroblast cells.
the development of combination therapy using copper complexes with phenoxazine derivatives as an effective and safe approach to cancer treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of a copper–thio- semicarbazone with a phenoxazine results in a significant enhancement in cytotoxicity against MCF-7 cells and that this combination approach is more effective than combinations with isoelectronic analogs.
this combination approach is effective in enhancing the cytotoxic potential against MCF-7 cells while maintaining a high degree of safety against normal fibroblast cell lines.

the combination of copper–thiose-micarbazone and phenoxazine results in a selective increase in intracellular reactive oxygen production and subsequent apoptotic cell death against the MCF7 cell line, with a reduced effect on normal fibroblast cell line (MRC- 5).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of copper–thiosemincarbazone complexes and phenoxazines is a promising approach for the treatment of breast cancer.

a combination therapy using a copper–thio-semicarbazone complex in conjunction with a phenoxazine is a novel strategy to increase the therapeutic potential of the copper–tio-semicar-bazone complex while minimizing the toxicity to normal cells.

the combination of copper–thiosemi-carbazone complexes and phenoxazines results, in the case of the benzophenoxazines, in a significant reduction in the copper–thiosemi-carbazone component of a combination therapy, while retaining the cytotoxic potential against cancer cells, and enhancing selectivity against cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of copper complexes with phenoxazine derivatives can be used to selectively enhance the efficacy of copper–thio-semicarbazone anticancer drugs against cancer cells while minimizing their toxic effects on normal cells.
combination therapy with copper–thiosemicarbazone compounds and phenoxazine compounds can be a viable option in the treatment of cancer.

the combination of copper–thio-semicarbazone anticancer complexes with phenoxazine compounds provides a means to enhance the cytotoxic potential and reduce the toxicity profile of the anticancer complexes.
